questions.q: A requirement states access should be granted 'only while a record is in a specific status, and automatically revoked once it leaves that status.' Which mechanism is purpose-built for this?
options: A criteria-based sharing rule
Apex managed sharing, creating and deleting a __Share record as status changes
Raising the object's OWD to Public Read/Write
A Restriction Rule
questions.explain: Apex managed sharing is the mechanism that can both grant and explicitly revoke access programmatically as a record's status changes — something a standard declarative sharing rule can't express on its own.

questions.q: A requirement says a narrow subset of records must be hidden from a group that would otherwise have access through role hierarchy and sharing rules alike. Which mechanism fits?
options: A public group
A sharing rule with broader criteria
A Restriction Rule
Raising OWD for the object
questions.explain: Restriction Rules are the one mechanism in this course's toolkit that removes visibility on top of whatever access a user would otherwise have, regardless of which other mechanism granted it.

questions.q: A per-deal, cross-departmental group of people needs record-level access to one specific Opportunity, with membership that changes deal by deal. What's the best fit?
options: An Opportunity Team
A standing public group shared by a sharing rule
Lowering Opportunity's OWD to Public Read/Write
Enterprise Territory Management
questions.explain: Teams exist specifically for per-record, per-deal groups whose membership doesn't map to a fixed population, role, or territory — exactly this scenario's shape.

questions.q: A detail object in a master-detail relationship needs its visibility to automatically follow its parent record, with no separate sharing decision per child record. What explains this behavior?
options: A criteria-based sharing rule evaluated on the child object
A manual share applied to every child record
Apex managed sharing applied per child record
Controlled by Parent OWD combined with implicit sharing
questions.explain: Controlled by Parent OWD means the detail record's visibility exactly mirrors its parent's — access flows implicitly from the relationship, with no rule evaluated against the detail object itself.

questions.q: A company's underwriter-to-state assignments change company-wide a few times a year and don't track the management reporting structure. Which tool is the best fit, and why?
options: Enterprise Territory Management, because the axis is independent of the org chart and the Planning state lets each remap be validated before it goes live
Role hierarchy, because any geographic grouping should always be modeled as roles
A single org-wide Restriction Rule, because restriction rules are designed for geographic access
Public Read Only OWD, because it removes the need for any assignment logic at all
questions.explain: A frequently-changing, non-hierarchical axis like state assignment is the signature use case for Enterprise Territory Management, whose Planning state exists specifically to validate a remap before committing to it.
